bibliographic.title: LLMOps, AgentOps, and MLOps for Generative AI: A Comprehensive Review
bibliographic.venue: International Journal of Computer Applications Technology and Research Volume 14–Issue 07
bibliographic.citation_apa: Joshi, S. (2025). LLMOps, AgentOps, and MLOps for Generative AI: A Comprehensive review. International Journal of Computer Applications Technology and Research, 14(7), 1–11. https://doi.org/10.7753/IJCATR1407.1001

methodology.study_design: comprehensive literature review combining systematic review of articles and industry practices
methodology.sample_description: over 100 recent articles and industry practices
methodology.technology_context: MLOps, LLMOps, GenAIOps, AgentOps, agentic AI, generative AI, multi-agent systems

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a 2025 review focused on operational frameworks (MLOps, LLMOps, AgentOps) for generative and agentic AI, with explicit coverage of monitoring, debugging, observability, prompt management, hallucination mitigation, ethical considerations, and enterprise deployment. It aligns with operational/technical governance dimensions of the review scope but does not center conversational governance, chatbots, or regulated conversational oversight; only page 1 was available for appraisal.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter/page 1 was provided; full-text verification is needed for systematic review methodology transparency, conversational governance relevance, regulated-domain treatment, and claimed case studies.

appraisal.notes: The abstract and introduction clearly state review aims and contributions, including a claimed systematic review of over 100 articles. However, the provided text does not describe search strategy, databases, inclusion/exclusion criteria, quality appraisal of included studies, or limitations. Appraisal is therefore provisional and limited to page 1.

cerqual.explanation: The source appears coherent and potentially adequate as an operational review of LLMOps/AgentOps, but methodological detail is insufficient in the excerpt to support high confidence. Relevance to conversational governance in regulated settings is partial because the focus is AI operations rather than conversational oversight, contestation, or compliance workflows.

coding.theme: Operational frameworks for generative and agentic AI
coding.subtheme: Evolution from MLOps to LLMOps, GenAIOps, and AgentOps

synthesis.main_claim: The paper argues that operational practices for AI have evolved from MLOps to LLMOps and GenAIOps, and further to AgentOps for managing agentic AI, proposing an integrated framework and recommendations for enterprise-scale generative AI deployment.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a claimed systematic review of over 100 recent articles and industry practices, summarizes an integrated MLOps-LLMOps-AgentOps framework, presents case studies, and offers implementation guidelines for organizations adopting generative AI at scale.
synthesis.limitations: Provided evidence is limited to page 1; review methods, quality assessment, full findings, case study details, and explicit limitations are not visible in the supplied text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for the operational/technical governance layer of LLM and agentic AI systems, especially monitoring, debugging, observability, and lifecycle management; not suitable as central evidence for conversational governance unless later sections directly address chatbots, human oversight, or regulated conversational controls.
